abstract: Open-ended conversational AI requires learners to formulate questions, organize learning paths, and track changing problem states. Structured visual interfaces may ease these demands, but higher average ratings do not establish that support is experienced consistently across learner backgrounds and devices. We conducted a randomized study of graph-algorithm learning, comparing VisualCodeChat (VCC), which combines predefined learning stages, conversational explanations, and dynamic algorithm visualizations, with a standard text-based chatbot. We analyzed 282 post-task questionnaires from university students. In unadjusted comparisons, VCC received significantly higher usability and perceived effectiveness ratings. We detected no significant between-condition differences in efficiency, satisfaction, or post-use emotion. Exploratory within-condition analyses identified differences associated with prior chatbot experience: infrequent users reported lower adoption and learning-management ratings in the standard AI condition, while uncomfortable prior chatbot experiences were associated with lower interaction and layout ratings in the VCC condition. These findings suggest that improving the average interaction experience is only part of making AI-supported learning inclusive. Future evaluations should examine whether learners with different prior experiences can obtain guidance, recover from difficulties, and demonstrate understanding independently across devices.

ur.ai_reason: 随机实验评估视觉AI学习界面的可用性与公平
ur.tldr: 随机比较结构化可视化聊天机器人与文本机器人辅助图算法学习。结构化界面总体可用性和感知有效性更高，但效率、满意度及情绪无显著差异；不同聊天机器人经验者表现分化，平均收益掩盖了使用与设备方面的包容性风险。

title: Beyond Average Gains: Probing the Equity--Vulnerability Tension in Structured Visual AI for Learning
title_zh: 超越平均学习增益：探析用于学习的结构化视觉AI中的公平—脆弱性张力
